descriptionChirho: Hiphil: to obtain, bring out, or furnish something good, especially divine favor. Used primarily in Proverbs: 'he who finds wisdom obtains favor from YHWH' (Prov 8:35, 18:22), 'the one who obtains understanding' (Prov 3:13), and 'a good man obtains favor from YHWH' (Prov 12:2). Arabic uses نَالَ/يَنالُ (to obtain/attain), Korean 얻다/얻는다 (to obtain), Spanish obtener (to obtain), Hindi प्राप्त करना (to obtain/acquire). The auto-clusters 'and obtains', 'obtains', 'who obtains' are identical Hiphil imperfect/consecutive forms with no semantic distinction -- all refer to obtaining or acquiring something beneficial, typically divine goodwill.

Hiphil: to furnish, provide, or pour out for another, extending the 'bring forth' meaning to active giving or supplying. In Ps 144:13, flocks 'providing' (מְפִיקִים) thousands in the fields, and in Isa 58:10, 'you shall offer/pour out (וְתָפֵק) your soul to the hungry.' Arabic مُفِيضَةٌ (overflowing/abundant) for Ps 144:13 and تُفرِغُ (to pour out) for Isa 58:10, Korean 내놓는다 (put forth) and 내면 (if you put forth), Spanish proveyendo (providing) and ofreces (you offer), Hindi देनेवाले (givers/providers) and देगा (will give). This sense emphasizes outward provision or generous giving rather than personal acquisition.

Hiphil jussive: to promote, advance, or cause to succeed, used of furthering the plans or desires of the wicked. In Ps 140:8, the psalmist prays 'do not promote (תָּפֵק) his devices,' asking God not to let the wicked's schemes prosper. Arabic تُقَدِّمْ (to advance/promote), Korean 이루어지게 마소서 (do not let it be accomplished), Spanish hagas prosperar (cause to prosper), Hindi सफल होने दे (let succeed). This sense is semantically distinct from 'obtain' and 'provide' because the subject causes another's plans to advance rather than obtaining something for oneself or furnishing goods to others.
